children: The early popularity of Meta's

Muse, an artificial intelligence agent that executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf, could generate even more demand for inference-related computing power if it takes hold, according to analysts.

"The market has been hyper-focused on the Enterprise AI market," said Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney in an investor note. "Excessively focused, we believe. We get it. Enterprises pay for productivity. Consumers don't. Or at least that's what the market assumes."
However, Muse changes that, as the product is directly marketed at consumers, and has been received positively. It ranks as the No. 1 free app download on Apple's
App Store and Google
Play. The app achieved nearly 750,000 U.S. iOS installs within five days of its release.

"This is an aggressively early call, but Muse IS the product cycle catalyst that can unlock shares and drive a re-rating to 25x ($810 on our ’27 estimates) or even 30x ($975), very much in the way that the successful Gemini 3 launch did with GOOGL shares last year," Mahaney added.
This would not only prove positive for Meta, but also for the hardware providers that make the running of agentic AI possible.
"The success of Meta's Muse shows a pivot toward continuous agentic workloads, creating a massive inference demand catalyst for companies like Nvidia
and AMD
, networking providers like Broadcom
, and memory producers like Micron
," said Seeking Alpha analyst
. "But, of course, in my opinion, it's too early to know what the use cases for these agents will actually be in the long-term."
Meanwhile,
, Investing Group Leader for Tech Contrarians, believes it could substantially benefit builders of Arm-based CPUs.

"Muse is the market's first real confrontation with consumer agentic AI, and while much remains unproven, successful adoption will have the biggest implications for the CPU scene," according to Tech Stock Pros. "Currently, the CPU-to-GPU ratio is roughly 1:4 to 1:8. With the success of agentic AI, it could shift closer to 1:1 to 1:2. This is part of why we saw the market reward CPU players with Muse's record downloads this Monday.

"Out of the bunch, we think Arm-based CPUs are best positioned to benefit, more so than the x86 market, with a perf-per-watt advantage. Also worth noting: if consumer agentic AI adoption sticks with Muse, we think this could create an entirely new competitive consumer-focused landscape that includes Apple and its new Siri."

And, of course, its success would also bode well for Meta. Evercore reiterated its Outperform rating and $860 price target on the stock following the Muse release. Mizuho also retained its Outperform rating and $750 target.

"We see the Meta bull case increasingly playing out, with strong momentum on adoption with Muse moving firmly to #1 in the app store, a Connector Platform introduced, more AI products/tie-ins coming at Meta Connect 2026 and the stock working with room to run, in our view," said Mizuho analyst Lloyd Walmsley in a Tuesday note.
Meta Connect 2026 takes place from Sept. 23 to 24 at Meta's Menlo Park Campus.

title: Meta's Muse brings agentic AI to consumers; could prompt 'massive inference demand': analyst
